note:
CONTRACT CORRECTION, read against the code BEFORE implementing (2026-09-27). The intent names `src/flow/frame.ts:433` as writing an absence note to the record, and AC-2 builds on that — "the same class of record the frame already writes". THAT IS WRONG, and the defect is WIDER than the contract states. `Frame.reviewGate` writes nothing: it pushes a note into `FrameResult.notices` (frame.ts:434 for the absence, :440 for the human verdict) and presents it interactively. NOTHING CONSUMES `notices` — the only reader in the tree is a test (`src/flow/steps/__tests__/steps.test.ts:254`), so the frame presents those two notes and drops them. CORRECTED READING: the ABSENCE is unrecorded on EVERY path (frame, CLI `submit!`, `gate! --review`), not only on the CLI one, and the `human` verdict is unrecorded on every path too. AC-2 keeps its requirement — recorded on every path, ONCE — and now covers the frame as well; what changes is that there is no existing frame record to copy.

AC-3 READ, since it is the one AC that could be satisfied two ways: the BOUND is NOT written to the record. A bound is a property of the GATE (rejections >= the constant), not of a review — no review ran — so recording it would put an outcome in the log for something that did not happen, and a gate that reached the bound BEFORE this code existed (12/23 is exactly that) would still read blank. It is DERIVED in one place from the rejection events, which ARE the record, and it takes precedence over a recorded outcome, because when the worker is out what an earlier pass concluded is not the live fact. Everything else — accept, rework, human, absent — is a per-attempt fact and IS recorded.

Q1 resolved to its default: the outcome rides the ONE findings landing (an `outcome` field on the same `evidence` event the findings already land on), so one review stays one record and a reader can never see findings without their verdict. Q2 stands: no declared dependency on 12/24 — the record is written from the verdict the rule RETURNS, so a re-cut or added arm is covered by construction.

claims.statement: A `human` verdict lands an outcome — that a review RAN, its date, the anchor sha, the run id, the findings count and the reason the rule derived — through the ONE findings writer, the same event that carries the findings. Correcting the review's F2: the anchor is NOT a field of the outcome object, it is `evidence.anchorSha` on that same event — `landFindings(id, findings, {anchorSha})` writes it, documented at store.ts as 'the commit the findings were read at' — and the surface prints it in the findings header, `FINDINGS (a review's record — 1 pass, latest 2026-09-27, cited at 933f32f)`, produced at command-renderers.ts:241. The STANDING deliberately does not repeat it: the standing is the next-line sentence, one line, and the anchor is one line below it in the same card. The gate stays submitted, no rejection is burned and no decision event is written — commands.test.ts asserts the gate, the rejection count and the decision list are byte-identical and only the outcome is added.

The absence is recorded on every path, ONCE, and now names WHICH of the contract's four it was — each name is one place the worker stops. Correcting the review's F4 (its only gap): `unreachable` is no longer collapsed into `unavailable`. REVIEW_ABSENCES is ['unavailable','unreachable','unparseable','empty']; `unavailable` = the worker could not be BUILT and is the whole of attemptGateReview's catch (the seam throws before the worker exists, so the worker's own writer never runs — handlers.ts); `unreachable` = the call threw (gate-review.ts's catch around `abilities.llm.complete`); `unparseable`/`empty` = the reply. Both CLI doors (`submit!`, `gate! --review`) and the frame go through `runGateReview`, so no door can double-write. On F4's second half: the four `gate! --review` REFUSALS (`review-with-flag`, `review-not-confirm`, `review-takes-no-decision`, `review-no-submission`) deliberately write nothing — they are decided before `attemptGateReview` is called, so no review was requested and none can be absent; recording one would put a review's outcome on a node no review was asked about, which is the false record `outcomeShapeProblem` refuses. §7.11 now states this. On F5: the store-refusal branch is pinned by a new test — corrupt ledger, unparseable reply — asserting the reason survives and the sentence appends 'AND THE OUTCOME COULD NOT BE RECORDED (store-refused: …)'; no fifth name is invented, because the write IS what failed.

The bound is DERIVED from the rejection events where the other outcomes are stated, at no model-call cost, and takes precedence over any recorded outcome — `runGateReview` returns before the model call and `Commands.reviewStanding` checks the bound BEFORE the recorded outcome, so an earlier pass's conclusion can never outrank the live fact. Live read, re-run at this build: `ann brief 12-operate-loop/23-implementation-criterion-evidence` → 'next: AT THE BOUND' and 'AT THE BOUND — the review worker is out of rejections and no review will run here: 3 of 3 rejections are burned…'. The CLI's own test asserts `fetch` was never called for the bound.

The card and `ann brief` read the outcome FROM THE RECORD and print REVIEWED AND LEFT / AT THE BOUND / ABSENT as three distinct next-lines, composed ONCE in Commands.reviewStanding (`label` + `line`, typed literals so the sentence cannot drift) and printed verbatim at three call sites — correcting the review's F3, which could not see them because the diff excerpt cut those hunks: command-renderers.ts:654 fills the brief's `next:` slot from `brief.review.label` and :659 prints `brief.review.line` under it; the node card prints the same `line` at command-renderers.ts:242; and the page's next-line takes the standing FIRST, at ui.ts:507-508 (`var standing = (detail.brief || {}).review; if (standing) return standing.line;`), before the `decide-now` override — which is why the next-line stops claiming 'waiting on a decision'. No renderer re-derives anything from severities.

No new event type and no new state: the outcome rides the EXISTING findings landing as `evidence.outcome` on the same event, `deriveGateVerdict` stays the only thing that names an arm (the outcome RECORDS what the rule returned), and a deciding verdict is refused in `outcome` BY NAME at the writer so the record cannot restate a decision. The store's test loops all four absence names as accepted and refuses a fifth.
